content: I was wondering if anyone might have a copy of Types and Programming Languages by Benjamin C. Pierce and would be willing to answer a question about a proof given in the text?
I have a copy and may be able to answer

Thank you.
The author points out that the proof given for Proposition 3.2.6, T=S, makes use of complete induction, but it seems to me that it could have been done with ordinary induction (Axiom 2.4.1). Did I perhaps miss something?

I seem to have formalized that a while ago (quite poorly though) here. 3.2.1 is roughly Term and 3.2.3 is S on line 41. The inductive definition in Lean is only an analogue of "some set S' that satisfies the three conditions in 3.2.1", however I think that induction is not needed here. This is reflected in my term_equiv_all_terms proof on line 84 which just uses Subtype.val. There is also a version using string encoding starting on line 202. Sorry for the confusing code in advance!
